newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche top manager welcomes US rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche top manager welcomes US rate rise.

text.p: Deutsche Bank management board member Ulrich Cartellieri on Wednesday welcomed Tuesday's U.S. interest rate rise but said that it was important now that the Bundesbank continued its policy of low interest rates.

"The interest rate rise was necessary to prevent an overheating of U.S. financial markets and to let the U.S. economy remain on a steady course for as long as possible. It is to be welcomed," he said.

But he added a continuation of the Bundesbank's low interest rate policy was necessary even with rising U.S. rates. Low interest rates were "one of the only supports" for the German economy which remained under pressure from weak domestic investment and high taxes.
The U.S. Federal Reserve raised its federal funds rate target by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent on Tuesday for the first time in more than two years.
The German central bank's key discount rate is at a historically low 2.50 percent.
